regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like acceleration — but IIP overall slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%, and core sector decelerated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%. The PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led (54.5) while manufacturing slipped to 52.8; goods-economy proxies are softening beneath a services-driven headline. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is the one number that earns optimism — it's at the 74th percentile and rising, which means the capex signal is real, not budgeted.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY is above RBI's 4% target, but the decomposition is the story: core CPI at 3.9% YoY sits at only the 28th percentile — demand-side inflation is contained. The entire overshoot is fuel: 22.93% YoY at the 95th percentile, driven by Brent near $99/bbl. The danger is second-order — fuel feeds into transport costs, which feed into food logistics, which feed into CFPI already at 5.52% YoY. RBI's own forecast has moved to 5.1% YoY; the repo at 5.25% p.a. is barely positive in real terms and offers no buffer if crude breaches $100.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Credit growth at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth at 10.8% YoY — a 630 bps divergence — keeps the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits, the 75th percentile historically. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo was being held flat, the system eventually hit a funding wall; NBFCs compensated then too, as they are now (14.9% YoY, up from 10.6%). Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month is at the 0th percentile — the wholesale funding alternative is essentially closed. If deposit growth doesn't accelerate to close even half the gap, expect RBI to tighten risk weights on specific lending categories before year-end.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is flat and at the 38th percentile historically — accommodative relative to where inflation is printing. With RBI's own inflation forecast now at 5.1% YoY, the real repo rate is barely 15 bps positive, which is insufficient to anchor expectations if fuel inflation persists. The policy bind: cutting would widen the CAD via INR depreciation and worsen imported inflation; holding risks being behind the curve if core CPI starts absorbing fuel pass-through. The RBI is not driving — it is being driven by Brent.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — rising from 75.6% — is the cleanest bullish signal in today's data. Credit to industry at 20% YoY and credit to services at 22.9% YoY confirm that financing is flowing into productive investment, not just consumption. The inversion: core sector growth slowing to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% means the upstream inputs to capex (steel, cement, power) are moderating. If core sector stays below 6% for two more months, the IIP capital goods print will follow with a lag.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a strong print, but at the 71st percentile — not a record, and the FYTD at ₹10,42,757 cr is at only the 14th percentile, suggesting the full-year run-rate is not exceptional. Passenger vehicles at 16% YoY, two-wheelers at 19.7% YoY, and commercial vehicles at 16.88% YoY show broad-based demand — two-wheeler strength in particular signals rural and semi-urban recovery, not just urban affluent spending. The inversion: credit card growth at only 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) while personal loans grow at 16.2% YoY suggests consumers are borrowing longer-term rather than revolving short-term — either a sign of confidence or of stretched budgets refinancing.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 630 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months: deposits lagging credit acceleration signals funding stress. NBFC credit growth at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% prior) shows non-bank lenders compensating, but wholesale funding dependency rising.","implication":"Overweight private sector banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity tightening will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 FY27 to ease deposit pressure, not inflation. Position for 50-75 bps of cuts by September.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile is historically a precursor to either deposit acceleration or credit slowdown. Last time it was this elevated (2022), RBI cut rates 250 bps within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month) is at 74th percentile — the sweet spot for capex acceleration without overheating. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior) is moderating but still positive. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (up from 6.5% prior) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2% prior) confirm broad-based capex financing.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers, cement, and steel. Domestic capex cycle will drive earnings growth for 18-24 months. Avoid imported capex plays — INR weakness at 96.15 ₹/USD (91st percentile high) will inflate equipment costs. Favour companies with 60%+ domestic sourcing.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the historical inflection point where capex accelerates. This level preceded 3-year bull runs in 2003-05 and 2014-16.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (up from 31,961 ₹ cr / month prior month) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 92nd percentile. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn) at 82nd percentile. But SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr) is at 93rd percentile — AUM growing faster than account growth. Average ticket size rising: AUM ÷ accounts = ₹18.6 lakh cr ÷ 100.18 mn = ₹1.86 lakh per account, up from ₹1.84 lakh prior month. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (86th percentile) with DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (100th percentile — all-time high).","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour: affluent retail entering, not mass-market SIP. Domestic institutional money (DII) at record levels suggests portfolio rebalancing into equities. Overweight large-cap quality and dividend payers — they will absorb DII flows. Underweight small-cap and growth — they will underperform when DII rotation completes. Expect volatility spike when FII reverses (currently at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month, 83rd percentile).","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile preceded market corrections in 2018 and 2022. Rising average ticket size is a contrarian signal — it marks the end of retail enthusiasm, not the beginning.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Credibility","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% prior month) is at 95th percentile — the highest in the dataset. Brent crude at 99.05 $/bbl (69th percentile) and WTI at 93.6 $/bbl (79th percentile) are both rising. Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY (up from 4.38% prior) with core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile, low) shows inflation is commodity-driven, not demand-driven. RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (up from 4.6% prior) signals RBI expects further overshoot. Repo rate flat at 5.25% p.a. (38th percentile historically low).","implication":"RBI is trapped: headline inflation above 4.5% target but core inflation benign. Rate cuts will be delayed until fuel inflation moderates. Hedge INR weakness (currently 96.15 ₹/USD, 91st percentile) — oil imports will worsen CAD. Overweight energy stocks and underweight rate-sensitive sectors (autos, housing). Expect RBI to hold rates through Q2 FY27, cutting only in Q3 if fuel inflation breaks.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile last occurred in 2022 and 2008 — both preceded sharp rupee depreciation and RBI emergency tightening.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"BOJ Tightening Unwinds Carry; DXY Steady","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1% p.a. (up from 0.75% prior, 86th percentile high) signals aggressive tightening. Fed funds at 3.63% p.a. (flat, 67th percentile mid) and US 10Y Treasury at 5.17% yield (down from 5.18%, 94th percentile high) show US rates sticky. DXY at 101.231 index (flat, 53rd percentile mid) is holding despite BOJ tightening — unusual. US PMI composite at 56 index (84th percentile high) vs China PMI at 49.5 index (47th percentile mid) shows divergence. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2% prior) signals EZ tightening bias.","implication":"Carry trade unwind risk is real but contained: DXY not rallying despite BOJ tightening suggests yen weakness is structural, not cyclical. Monitor for sudden DXY spike above 102 — that would trigger forced deleveraging in emerging markets. India's INR at 96.15 ₹/USD (91st percentile) is already pricing in carry unwind. Reduce leverage in EM equities; overweight India defensives (FMCG, pharma) over cyclicals.","pct_10y":53,"pct_note":"DXY at 53rd percentile mid is historically neutral. BOJ at 86th percentile high is a regime shift — last time was 2019, which preceded 18-month yen strength.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates; RBI Defending Quietly","data_text":"INR at 96.15 ₹/USD (up from 95.97 ₹/USD prior month, 91st percentile high) — rising 3 of last 5 months. Recent trend: 95.24 → 94.34 → 95.24 → 96.15 → 95.24 → 96.15 shows volatility but clear depreciation bias. FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (83rd percentile) is strong but reversing from -3,111.9 ₹ cr net / month two months prior — flow volatility is high. Brent crude at 99.05 $/bbl and fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY will worsen India's CAD. US 10Y Treasury at 5.17% yield (94th percentile high) keeps carry attractive for foreign investors, but BOJ tightening at 1% p.a. (86th percentile) is unwinding yen carry.","implication":"RBI is likely intervening to defend 96 ₹/USD but will lose this battle if oil stays above 100 $/bbl. Expect INR to trade 96.5-97.5 ₹/USD by Q2 FY27. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, textiles) — they benefit from INR weakness. Underweight importers (autos, capital goods) — input costs rising. Hedge FX exposure for corporates; INR volatility will spike if FII reverses.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile high is a 10-year extreme. Last time INR was this weak (2022), it depreciated another 8% before stabilising.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter (up from 12.8 mn sq ft prior quarter) appears positive, but the 10-year percentile is 6% lo — this is a 10-year low. Recent trend reveals the trap: 48 → 29.9 → 26.9 → 13.2 → 4.9 → 11.6 mn sq ft / quarter shows a 5-quarter collapse from 48 mn to 11.6 mn. Meanwhile, Nifty IT is flat (recent: 23,271 → 23,346 → 23,414 → 23,329 → 23,447 → 23,141), and retail mall vacancy at 5% vacant (down from 7.5%, 84th percentile strong-positive) shows retail RE is recovering. Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (down from 16.1%, 42nd percentile mid) masks the real story: absorption is collapsing because Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses, not because IT services demand is weak. Rent in Bengaluru at 100.6 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 94 ₹/sqft/mo, 57th percentile mid) and Mumbai at 125 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 117.9 ₹/sqft/mo, 38th percentile lo) are rising despite absorption collapse — this is a supply-demand mismatch, not a demand crisis.","implication":"Do NOT short IT services on office absorption data. GCCs are consolidating into trophy assets (Mumbai CBD, Bengaluru Whitefield) and exiting secondary markets. Overweight large-cap IT (TCS, Infosys, HCL) — they control prime real estate and will benefit from consolidation. Underweight mid-cap IT and IT parks — they will face secular headwinds as GCCs right-size. Commercial RE play: buy into Mumbai CBD and Bengaluru Grade-A office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) — they will capture GCC consolidation. Avoid secondary office parks and IT SEZs.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is a 10-year low, but this is a structural shift (GCC consolidation), not a cyclical downturn. The last time absorption was this low (2020 COVID), it recovered in 18 months. This time, recovery will be slower and concentrated in trophy assets.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry the Headline — Goods Economy Quietly Slows

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is services-driven: PMI Services rose to 54.5 while PMI Manufacturing slipped to 52.8 (48th percentile).
  • IIP overall decelerated to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%; core sector slowed to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — goods-economy momentum is fading.
  • But capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) is the one indicator that earns optimism — investment cycle has real underpinning.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY signal rural demand recovery; credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) suggests urban consumers are stretching budgets, not splurging.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY and PMI above 54 suggest expansion; IIP deceleration and core sector softening say the goods economy is losing the plot. Services cannot sustain the headline indefinitely if manufacturing and upstream inputs are both slowing.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: a third consecutive print below 5.5% would signal that IIP capital goods strength is borrowed time.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Surveys Say Expansion — Bond Market Says Otherwise

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 56 (84th percentile) and S&P 500 at all-time 100th-percentile 7,684 price re-acceleration.
  • But US GDP SAAR slowed to 1.5% SAAR from 2.1%; US 10Y Treasury at 5.17% yield (94th percentile) is doing the Fed's tightening for it.
  • China PMI at 49.5 (contraction) with GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0%) removes the commodity-reflation backstop for EM.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is unwinding yen carry — DXY at 101.2 holding despite this is the anomaly to watch.

The tension: Equity markets are pricing a soft landing; bond markets at 94th-percentile yields and decelerating nominal GDP are pricing something harder. China's inability to reflate means the global growth bridge that EM relied on is narrowing.

Bottom line: BOJ is the underappreciated tail risk: if yen carry unwinds accelerate, EM equity outflows follow within 60 days — watch USD/JPY as the leading indicator.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Conviction at Record Highs — Funding Plumbing Under Stress

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising two consecutive months); DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month — an all-time 100th-percentile print.
  • SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile) growing faster than accounts (100.18 mn, 82nd percentile) — average ticket rising to ₹1.86 lakh per account from ₹1.84 lakh.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile) — but the recent sequence was -₹3,112 cr two months prior; flow volatility is high.
  • But corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month is at the 0th percentile — wholesale funding markets are effectively shut, forcing NBFCs onto bank credit lines.

The tension: Retail liquidity via SIPs is structurally strong and deepening; institutional wholesale funding is at a decade low. The system is liquid at the top and stressed at the pipes — NBFCs dependent on bank credit lines face a squeeze if CD ratio tightening triggers macro-prudential action.

Bottom line: If RBI issues a risk-weight circular on NBFC lending, bank credit to NBFCs (currently 14.9% YoY) will compress sharply — that is the liquidity event to hedge.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty Cracks, REITs Bleed — NRI Demand Holds the Residential Floor

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING: NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up from 15%, +5 pp), with 25% share within premium/luxury — remittances at $135.46 bn (14% YoY) provide the hard-currency floor.
  • Supply is skewing luxury: ultra-luxury (>₹2.5 cr) and luxury (₹1.5–2.5 cr) together account for 47% of new launches; affordable (6% — a structural mismatch with mass-market demand.
  • Bank Nifty at 54,472 (89th percentile) fell from 55,580 — the first meaningful pullback in six sessions; India VIX jumped to 13.6 from 12.2, a 12% single-session spike.
  • Office REITs pricing the absorption collapse: Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit (down from ₹438), Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down from ₹508), Brookfield at ₹263/unit (down from ₹338) — all down 15–32% from prior prints.

The tension: NRI demand and SIP-driven DII flows are supporting asset prices from below; Bank Nifty's pullback at the 89th percentile and a VIX spike suggest institutional positioning is turning cautious. REIT valuations have already repriced the office absorption collapse — residential has not.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until GCC campus consolidation stabilises absorption above 20 mn sq ft / quarter; residential premium segment supported by NRI flows — overweight developers with luxury exposure in MMR and Bengaluru.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Crude Is the Common Thread

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $99.05/bbl: a $5 move through $100 widens CAD by ~40 bps, pushes CPI toward RBI's 5.1% YoY forecast ceiling, and forces a policy rethink — probability high, impact severe.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with corporate bond issuance at 0th percentile: if deposit growth stays at 10.8% YoY while credit runs at 17.1% YoY, a macro-prudential tightening circular arrives before Q3 results — probability medium, impact high.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. unwinding yen carry with US 10Y at 5.17% yield: if DXY breaks above 103, FII flows reverse and INR tests 97–98 — probability medium, impact medium-high.
  • But India VIX at 13.6 (9th percentile) means options are cheap — the market is not pricing any of these risks into hedges yet.

The tension: All three risks share a crude-oil trigger: Brent above $100 simultaneously worsens CAD, delays rate cuts, and pressures INR — the feedback loop is tighter than consensus pricing suggests.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude daily: a close above $100/bbl this week triggers the CAD-INR-inflation feedback loop and makes the RBI's 5.25% p.a. repo untenable as a hold.

"}
